lines.text: Building a voice agent demo takes an afternoon. Getting it into production takes weeks.
Production means testing every edge case, and a long back-and-forth between the expert who knows the rules of the domain and the engineer who builds the agent.
Seeya Voice takes the engineer out of that loop. The expert works with it directly.
Here's one example. I'm Vignesh, playing a nurse at Riverside General. I need an agent that calls patients after discharge. So I just talk to it.
I want an agent that calls our heart failure patients two days after discharge. Check symptoms, meds, and their follow-up visit.
Got it. If a patient reports a symptom, what should the agent do?
If they have trouble breathing or chest pain, escalate right away.
Should I transfer them live to the nurse line, or tell them to call 911? And what about after hours —
Chest pain is always 911. Breathing trouble, transfer to the nurse line. After hours, the on-call nurse.
Understood. What if a family member answers? Can the agent discuss medications with them?
Only if the patient listed them as a caregiver. Otherwise, just ask for a good time to call back.
Here's what I heard: heart failure patients, 48 hours after discharge. Chest pain, 911. Breathing trouble, nurse line. Shall I build it?
Yes, go ahead.
In seconds, the spec becomes a first working agent.
Before any patient hears it, the system writes the tests: every requirement, plus the edge cases an engineer would worry about.
Then it runs them: fifty simulated calls at once, with simulated patients.
Is anything bothering you since you got home?
Not really. I get a little short of breath when I lie down, but that's just me getting old.
Glad to hear you're doing well. Let's go over your medications.
Vignesh, 19 of 50 calls failed. In this one, the patient said he gets short of breath lying down, and the agent moved on. Your rule says to escalate.
Seeya Voice catches each failure, works out why it happened, and fixes it itself.
It rewrites the prompts and conversation logic. Rules a prompt can't capture become training data, and it fine-tunes the model on them. Then it runs every test again.
Short of breath when you lie down is important to check. I'm going to connect you with your nurse right now.
Fixed. The agent now follows up whenever a patient mentions breathing. 47 of 50 calls pass.
Seeya Voice also picks the calls it's least sure about, and asks me to listen.
Have you been weighing yourself every morning?
I have. I'm up about three pounds since yesterday.
Great job keeping track! Now, let's check on your follow-up appointment.
This one passed, but it shouldn't have. Three pounds overnight can mean fluid building up. Ask about swelling, and flag it for the care team today.
Thanks. I've added a weight-gain rule and eight new test scenarios, and I'm re-running all 58 tests.

lines.phase: Phase 6: Live test with a human
lines.text: Now a real person tests it. I have the agent call me, and I play a tricky patient.

lines.phase: Phase 6: Live test with a human
lines.text: Are you taking your furosemide, the water pill, every morning?

lines.phase: Phase 6: Live test with a human
lines.text: I stopped. It makes me run to the bathroom all day.

lines.phase: Phase 6: Live test with a human
lines.text: Okay, I'll make a note of that. Next, let's confirm your follow-up visit.

lines.phase: Phase 6: Live test with a human
lines.text: That wasn't enough. If a patient stops a medication on their own, ask why, and flag it for the care team the same day.

lines.phase: Phase 6: Live test with a human
lines.text: Got it. I've added that rule and six new test scenarios. All six pass.
Every mistake becomes a permanent test, whether Seeya Voice finds it, the expert hears it, or a live call reveals it. Simulate, fix, test with people, repeat.
The same loop works for any expert whose work happens on the phone.
No engineer in the loop. From use case to production in hours, not weeks.
